description:
Advances: specled.tag_scanning

Severity: Low (calibrated in the 2026-08-12 consolidated critical review of specled_-c5b, finding F11).

specled_-c5b taught process_statement/4 to recurse into for-comprehension bodies. The same blindness remains for other module-level constructs that can wrap test definitions: an if/unless block, and a for..reduce: body. Each silently drops any @tag spec inside it — no tag entry and no dynamic entry — which is the same tagged_tests_cover_missing_tag false positive c5b was filed to eliminate, in narrower shapes.

Why this could not land on the c5b branch: it needs an unmade design decision about which node types the scanner recurses into, and the two cases differ. An if/unless else branch is genuinely ambiguous — statements in both branches are visible to the parser but only one runs, so recursing into both may over-report carriers. A for..reduce: body is a clause list of {:->, _, _} rather than a do block, so it does not fit the block_from_args/block_statements shape the other clauses share and would need its own handling.

No adopter evidence yet that either shape is used to define tagged tests, unlike the for-comprehension case which was demonstrated in a real adopter sweep. Worth deciding deliberately rather than extending the recursion reflexively.
title: TagScanner drops tests defined under module-level if/unless and for..reduce: bodies
